mcp.title: Model Context Protocol
mcp.subtitle: Connect AI coding assistants to Aexy

overview.heading: Overview
overview.descriptionAfter: lets AI assistants like Claude Code, Claude Desktop and OpenAI Codex interact directly with your Aexy workspace — managing sprints, querying analytics, running agents, and more through natural language.

step1.title: Create an API token
step1.description: Generate a token to authenticate the MCP server with your Aexy account.

step2.title: Pick your client
step2.description: The server runs through uvx, so there is nothing to clone or keep updated — your client fetches it on demand.

step3.title: Add the configuration
step3.description: Copy the block for your client below into the file it names, then restart the client.

intro.claudeCode: Either run the CLI command, or commit the project file so everyone on the repo gets the server. Both are equivalent; the CLI writes to your user config, the file is shared.
intro.claudeDesktop: Claude Desktop reads a single config file. Create it if it does not exist, then quit and reopen the app — it only loads this file at startup.
intro.chatgpt: ChatGPT connects to remote MCP servers over HTTP.
intro.codex: Codex reads MCP servers from its TOML config. Add this table, then restart Codex.
intro.cursor: Cursor and VS Code use the same stdio server with slightly different file shapes. Use whichever matches your editor.
intro.other: Any MCP client that supports the stdio transport can run the server with this shape. Translate it into whatever format your client expects.

remoteRequired.heading: Not available yet
remoteRequired.body: ChatGPT only supports remote MCP servers reached over HTTP with OAuth — it cannot launch a local stdio process the way Claude Code, Claude Desktop and Codex do. Aexy's hosted MCP endpoint is in progress; until it ships, use one of the other clients.

env.apiToken: Your API token, created in Settings → API Tokens
